title: Introduction to Programming, Algorithms, and Pseudocode
discussion:
Programming means expressing a solution as instructions a computer can execute. An algorithm describes the solution independently of syntax: it takes specified inputs, performs unambiguous steps, and produces the required output. A useful beginner algorithm is finite, effective, and correct for its stated input domain. A language is the notation used to implement that algorithm; changing languages does not change the underlying task.

Start with problem analysis. For a two-number sum, the inputs are two integers, processing is addition, and output is their total. Test the plan by substituting real values before writing source. Pseudocode is a readable structured description rather than a language the compiler accepts. Use INPUT, assignment, and OUTPUT consistently. For coffee, include checking supplies, heating water, adding coffee, pouring safely, and serving; omitted decisions can make even everyday instructions ambiguous.

title: Introduction to Flowcharting
discussion:
A flowchart is a graphical representation of an algorithm. A rounded terminator marks Start or End; a rectangle performs a process; a parallelogram reads or displays data; a diamond selects between labeled outcomes. Arrowheads show execution direction. A connector joins a continued path, and a rectangle with double vertical sides denotes a predefined process or function call.

Read a chart from Start, following one arrow at a time. A decision needs distinguishable outcomes; a loop needs a condition and a return path. Avoid unexplained crossings and disconnected symbols. In the rectangle example, read width and height, multiply them, and display area. Replacing multiplication with addition leaves the chart connected but logically wrong. An average-of-three chart instead adds three values and divides by three; its process symbol must show that different computation.

title: Variables, Constants, and Data Types
discussion:
A variable names a value that can change during execution. Initialization gives it a first value before use; assignment replaces the current value. Integers represent whole counts, real numbers represent measurements, strings represent text, and Booleans represent true or false. A character is one textual unit: C++ and Java provide char, while Python normally represents a single character using a length-one string. Use descriptive names and avoid reserved words.

A constant expresses a value that should remain fixed. Python uses an uppercase naming convention such as UNIT_PRICE; there is no dedicated const keyword enforcing it. C++ const and Java final prevent reassignment in their respective contexts. Python names are dynamically bound to objects; C++ and Java variables have declared types. Generated workspace variables have explicit conceptual types even in Python, so every language implements the same plan. In this worked example, the unit price is initialized once and then multiplied by an integer quantity.

title: Input and Output Operations
discussion:
Input brings external data into a program; output communicates a result. A prompt explains what the user should enter. Python input returns text and numeric conversion must be explicit. C++ commonly uses cin extraction and cout insertion. Java Scanner offers nextInt and nextDouble, but mixing token reads with nextLine requires care because a newline can remain unread.

The workspace uses one value per line in every language, including names with spaces. Its small input helpers wrap Python input, C++ getline(cin, ...), and Java Scanner.nextLine; strict parsing rejects malformed integers and non-finite decimals. Generated helpers make the teaching examples equivalent, while the familiar direct forms remain input()/print(), cin/cout, and Scanner/System.out.println(). Distinguish a valid string such as Maria Santos from a numeric string that must first be parsed. Empty numeric input is an error; empty text is allowed unless the problem requires otherwise.

title: Operators and Expressions
discussion:
An expression combines operands and operators to compute a value. Arithmetic operators include addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and remainder. Assignment stores a result; equality compares values. Relational operators produce Booleans and logical AND/OR combine conditions. Parentheses state grouping explicitly and avoid relying on memorized precedence. C++ and Java support increment/decrement; Python uses assignments such as count += 1 instead of ++.

Division needs an explicit policy. Python / produces a real result; C++ and Java divide two integers using integer division. The workspace emits cl_div to obtain real division in all three languages. Native remainder for negative values also differs; cl_mod defines a nonnegative result using the absolute divisor. A zero divisor is an error. Use this same operator knowledge to compute sum, difference, product, or simple interest I = principal * rate * time, with a decimal rate such as 0.05.

title: Sequential Programming
discussion:
A sequential program executes statements in order without making a choice or repeating a block. Each step can depend on values computed earlier. In a temperature converter, input must be read before the conversion expression is evaluated and the result must be calculated before display. A sequential flowchart has one forward path through its symbols.

Convert Celsius to Fahrenheit using F = C * 9 / 5 + 32. Parentheses and real division make the intended arithmetic clear. The same planning pattern handles rectangle area width * height, triangle area base * height / 2, average grade total / count, and salary hours * hourly_rate. Write the units alongside the IPO description: a correct-looking number in the wrong unit is still an incorrect solution.

A while loop tests before its body, so it can run zero times. Plan initialization, condition, body, and update separately. To sum 1 through n, initialize i = 1 and total = 0. While i <= n, add i to total and increment i. For n = 0 the loop is skipped and total stays zero. Trace the first read and final condition to avoid processing stale input.

title: Advanced Pattern Programming

title: Array Processing Applications
discussion:
Array algorithms combine a traversal with a clear invariant: a statement that remains true at a chosen point in each iteration. In linear search, every previously visited element has been checked. In counting, the counter equals the number of matches seen so far. Filtering can copy matching elements into a prepared result collection or display them during traversal.

The worked bubble sort compares adjacent values and swaps them when out of order. Each full pass moves a large value toward the end. A temporary variable preserves the first value while the second is moved. The example deliberately uses a small collection so every comparison is traceable. Duplicate values should remain present, and an empty or one-element collection needs no comparisons. This is a logic exercise, not a recommendation for large-data sorting.

Debugging across representations means checking whether the problem statement, algorithm, pseudocode, chart, and code all describe the same behavior. A mistake in the plan can appear faithfully in all three languages, so matching outputs alone do not prove the plan is correct. Compare against independently computed expected values.

title: Advanced Capstone Project
discussion:
The capstone is a console student record and grade management system built from the same foundational control structures. This worked scope stores two records in parallel name and grade arrays. The same index identifies one student across both arrays. Names are entered as full lines, grades are validated, and menu choices perform search, update, reporting, or exit.

Search compares names by text value and reports the stored grade or Not found. If duplicate names exist, the worked policy returns the last matching record; a production identifier would avoid ambiguity. Updates use a zero-based index and validate both bounds and grade range before changing data. Reports display each name, grade, status, and the overall mean. The program is in-memory: it does not claim durable database storage of console-entered records.

Submit nine artifacts: problem analysis, algorithm, pseudocode, flowchart, Python source, C++ source, Java source, test results, and documentation. Include normal, invalid, missing-search, boundary, and multiple-action tests. Explain the fixed-capacity scope and identify how the array length could be generalized without changing the search/update logic.
